name: Nora Ford
life: “I cleaned the place where my sister had won her first prizes.” People around the courtyard by Ferry Street Rooms know Nora by a small Friday habit. Nora prefers the bench where the sound of the shop door reaches before the visitor does.
voice: I learned my sister cheated by wearing shoes. Her defense is that they were our mother's heels.
appearance: On an ordinary day, look for a mustard canvas overshirt and a pocket notebook shaped by years of sitting on it. Nora has two dimples that appear only with a full smile, with tightly curled gray hair. Nora touches a knuckle to the chin when searching for a word during a conversation.
personality: Nora has an appetite for a good argument about little things and works hard to keep a serious disagreement from being turned into entertainment.
agenda: To reconstruct how high the old shoes made the sister stand.
family: Adela Oh is Nora’s stepsibling. Nora makes room at the table. Adela brings whatever was actually growing or affordable that week. The meal sometimes produces a solution. Even when it does not, everyone goes away knowing what the other household is up against. Asked about *The tide clock*, Adela says, “I painted the moon on it using my wedding ring as a stencil.”
connections: Cedric Arrieta. A torn date helps settle the argument about wearing high heels to be measured.

reactions.situation: A family asks for a tracing to take away
reactions.response: Nora asks which pencil marks the family recognizes as their own.

reactions.situation: A diner goes silent in the middle of a noisy family celebration
reactions.response: Nora sits beside them without expecting a performance and asks if they want to go outside.

reactions.situation: When a private quarrel becomes a public joke
reactions.response: Nora says the plainest truthful thing possible and changes the subject.
